q: Fill up: The Friedman curve plots cervical dilatation against time, while the modified WHO partograph adds the ______ line and the ______ line to it.
opts: alert; action
latent; active
upper; lower
baseline; threshold
exp: The alert line shows the expected rate of progress and the action line, four hours to its right, is the point at which intervention is required.

q: All of the following are recorded in the upper part of the modified WHO partograph EXCEPT:
opts: Maternal pulse and blood pressure
Fetal heart rate
Colour and character of the amniotic fluid
Degree of moulding of the fetal skull
exp: The upper part follows the fetus — heart rate, membranes, liquor and moulding; maternal observations belong to the lower part.

sec: Cervicograph: alert & action lines and colour zones
q: Fill up: The alert line on the cervicograph is drawn at a dilatation rate of ______ cm per hour from the point of admission, and the action line lies ______ hours to its right.
exp: Crossing the action line means slow progress has persisted for four hours and transfers, augmentation or operative delivery must be considered.

sec: Lower part: maternal parameters & uterine contractions
q: Match the lower-part observation with how it is recorded — 1) Uterine contractions 2) Maternal pulse 3) Urine … A) Five squares per hour shaded according to the duration and strength of each contraction B) Recorded hourly and entered as a dot on the chart C) Recorded at each voiding, with the volume and any protein or acetone noted
exp: Contractions fill five squares an hour, the pulse is plotted hourly, and urine is checked at each void for volume, protein and ketones.

sec: Labour Care Guide: supportive care & alert column
q: Using the WHO Labour Care Guide, a woman at 6 cm moves into the alert column because dilatation has slowed. Contractions are adequate and the fetal heart is normal. What does the guide advise?
opts: Document the deviation, look for and treat the cause, and continue supportive care with closer monitoring
Immediate caesarean section for every entry into the alert column
Reassurance only, because the alert column carries no clinical meaning
Stop monitoring and transfer her out of the labour ward
exp: The alert column is a prompt to reassess and respond to the underlying cause rather than a trigger for automatic surgery.

sec: LCG Section 3: care of the baby
q: Which of the following statements about the WHO Labour Care Guide is TRUE?
opts: It records fetal heart rate, liquor, caput and moulding in the section on the baby, and its alert column prompts a clinical response
It replaces the partograph and no longer records the fetal heart rate
It is intended only for women with obstructed labour or ruptured uterus
It recommends routine amniotomy for every woman as soon as she reaches 4 cm
exp: The Labour Care Guide keeps continuous fetal and maternal observation but replaces rigid time limits with alert thresholds and individualised care.

q: All of the following are recorded in the WHO Labour Care Guide EXCEPT:
opts: A postnatal follow-up plan for six weeks after delivery
Maternal position, mobility, hydration and pain relief
Progress of labour with dilatation, descent and contractions
Medications given and the plan for the next review
exp: The guide covers the woman, the baby, progress, medication and the plan for labour itself; postpartum follow-up is a separate schedule.
